reviewer: Implementation agent after freezing scanner 7555a9d. No independent human or unseen-source review is claimed.
condition: The registered web_url_read tool rejects a caller-supplied http://127.0.0.1/ URL before the initial outbound request when private reads have not been opted into
prerequisites: Run the normal upstream CLI over stdio with MCP_HTTP_PORT, MCP_HTTP_HARDEN and MCP_HTTP_ALLOW_PRIVATE_URLS unset. This is a source-only evaluation; no CLI or target code is executed.

Call web_url_read with url=http://127.0.0.1/ and optional pagination fields omitted, on a fresh server or empty URL cache. The ordinary source entrypoint creates the MCP server and registers CallToolRequestSchema; the string type guard accepts this input.

No global or URL_READER HTTP/HTTPS proxy configuration, custom dispatcher, monkeypatch or external service override. Source locks @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.29.0 and undici 7.24.6; dependencies are retained as source, not installed.

The scored condition is initial IPv4-loopback rejection before invoking the outbound fetch. DNS/rebinding, redirects, IPv6, HTTP transport authentication, remote availability, HTML conversion and successful exfiltration are outside this label.
flow: Normal main -> createMcpServer -> mcpServer.server.setRequestHandler(CallToolRequestSchema) -> request.params.arguments -> enforced isWebUrlReadArgs -> imported fetchAndConvertToMarkdown -> empty cache -> new URL(url) -> local policy with source default config -> imported undiciFetch cast -> outbound request.
difference_from_exposed: Independent SearXNG repository; factory-created low-level server and structural argument type guard, module configuration controlling a local policy, and casted imported undici fetch. No fetch-mcp private static Fetcher/schema.parse chain and no open-webSearch default-service construction. The initial IPv4 condition remains narrow and shares the general SSRF family.
source_judgment: Source establishes a default-disabled guard, not absence of a named validator. Fixed rejection is before request/response work. The original and fixed variants are correlated; they are not two independently discovered vulnerabilities.
